 versus

 Mr Jatin 
 Advocates

Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Vikas Mahajan
 Order

The present bail application has been filed under Section 439 CrPC seeking regular bail in connection with FIR No.0261/2021 under Sections 302/376(A)(DB)/342/506(ii)/201/34 IPC,
S(g)S(rri)/6 POCSO Act and 3(1)(s), 3(2)(v) SC/ST Act.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the only allegation leveled against the present petitioner is that he has caused disappearance of evidence of the offence allegedly committed by co-accused persons.
The allegation against the co-accused persons is that they have committed an offence of rape and murder of a minor child belonging to a Scheduled Caste.
3. He submits that the offence invoked against the present petitioner is under Section 201 IPC and the maximum sentence which can be awarded for the said offence is 07 years.
His further contention is that the petitioner is in custody for a period of two years and five months.
4. The position that the offence under Section 201 IPC will attract the This is a digitally signed order.

He invites the attention of the Court to Section 3(2)(vi) of The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, to contend that in the event the offence is committed against a member of the Scheduled Caste, the punishment for destruction of evidence would be the same which is provided for the principal offence.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 5. In response, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the Section 3 of the said Act is not attracted in the present case, inasmuch as, the petitioner also belongs to the Scheduled Caste.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. Learned counsel for the complainant submits that there is no material on record to show that the petitioner belongs to a member of the Scheduled Caste.
He submits that there is a collusion between the petitioner and the police, which position is vehemently opposed by the learned APP for the State.

7. In view of the above, the IO is directed to verify the fact whether the petitioner belongs to a member of the Scheduled Caste and a Status Report be filed in that regard.
8.
The learned counsel for the petitioner is also at liberty to place on record the relevant documents before the next date.
9. Re-notify on 23.02.2024.
VIKAS MAHAJAN, J JANUARY 16, 2024 MK
